ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Evel Knievel

code.originalText: Hepatitis C confirmed with compensated cirrhosis: elastography, hepatology consultation, carvedilol for portal hypertension, statin, vaccines, and the antiviral plan

text.paragraph: Hepatitis C results and hepatology consultation. [S]

Mr. Knievel returns two weeks after his first visit. The hepatitis C antibody was positive and the reflex test found HCV RNA, 2.35 million IU/mL, genotype 1a. Hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody were all negative, so he has never had hepatitis B and is not immune; hepatitis A IgG was negative; HIV was negative. The ultrasound a week ago showed a nodular liver, a 14.2 cm spleen, no liver mass and no ascites. Dr. Okonkwo of hepatology saw him this morning, and transient elastography in her clinic measured liver stiffness at 26.8 kPa. He stopped ibuprofen and omeprazole after the first visit and uses acetaminophen twice a day and diclofenac gel on his knees; pain is a little worse in the mornings. He has cut down to about two drinks most evenings. He has had no abdominal swelling, black stools, vomiting of blood, confusion or yellow eyes. He has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

Raised transaminases (ALT 88, AST 96 U/L) and low platelets (118) on today's tests, with spider angiomas and palmar erythema, in a man of 57 who received many blood transfusions after crashes before 1992 and drinks most evenings: chronic liver disease, most likely hepatitis C, must be excluded. Hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis A and B serology, HIV, liver ultrasound and hepatology review ordered

list.item:
Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, treatment-naive (B18.2). Chronic hepatitis C, most likely from transfusions after his crashes before blood was screened for it. He is eligible for the AASLD-IDSA simplified pathway for compensated cirrhosis: no prior treatment, Child-Pugh A, eGFR above 30, hepatitis B surface antigen negative, no known liver cancer and no transplant. Dr. Okonkwo recommends sofosbuvir-velpatasvir, one tablet daily for 12 weeks, to start once it is approved. The interaction check is clean now that omeprazole has stopped; atorvastatin can be used with muscle-pain monitoring. [S]
Sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for 12 weeks when approved.
Avoid proton pump inhibitors during treatment; if acid treatment is needed, famotidine up to 40 mg twice a day taken with the tablet or 12 hours apart.
HCV RNA 12 or more weeks after the last dose.

Compensated cirrhosis, Child-Pugh A5, MELD-Na 8 (K74.69). FIB-4 above 3.25, liver stiffness above 12.5 kPa, a nodular liver, splenomegaly and platelets below 150 all point to cirrhosis, with alcohol as a cofactor. It is compensated. Cirrhosis carries a lifelong risk of liver cancer, so surveillance continues after cure. No transplant evaluation is needed now; referral would follow any decompensation or a MELD-Na of 15. [S]
Ultrasound with alpha-fetoprotein every six months, next in July.
Hepatitis A and B vaccines today.
Report abdominal swelling, black stools, vomiting of blood, confusion or yellow eyes the same day.

Clinically significant portal hypertension (K76.6). A liver stiffness of 25 kPa or more establishes clinically significant portal hypertension under Baveno VII. A non-selective beta-blocker lowers the risk of decompensation, and carvedilol is preferred; a patient who takes one does not need screening endoscopy for varices. [S]
Carvedilol 6.25 mg daily, raised to 12.5 mg at the next visit if systolic pressure stays above 100.
No screening endoscopy while he takes carvedilol.

Type 2 diabetes in cirrhosis (E11.65). A1c 7.4% in January; in cirrhosis the A1c can read falsely low, so a continuous glucose monitor will guide treatment. Metformin is safe in compensated cirrhosis with normal kidney function if he stops drinking. LDL 112 mg/dL: a statin is indicated for diabetes at his age and is safe in compensated cirrhosis. [S]
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily from today.
Continuous glucose monitor ordered.
Eye examination referral.

Raised transaminases and low platelets (R74.01). Explained by chronic hepatitis C with cirrhosis; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.

Call for abdominal swelling, black stools, vomiting of blood, confusion or yellow eyes.
